technical_facts: Ported Quake to Apple's Rhapsody (WWDC demo) using a codebase that merges QuakeWorld into Quake 2.
The port currently only supports network games.
The demo ran through 24-bit display postscript without assembly language compilation.
The direct-to-screen API in Rhapsody avoids the lock/unlock overhead associated with DirectDraw.
Sound access in Rhapsody avoids the penalties associated with DirectSound.
The port utilizes an existing openstep program from Omnigroup similar to qspy.
personality_patterns: Prone to rapid, high-intensity bursts of development ('stole some time', 'mostly last weekend - running tight').
Direct and honest communication style regarding performance claims and technical limitations.
Proactive and focused on long-term technical standards (pressing the OpenGL issue).
Rational and evidence-based decision making ('remaining decisions can be rationally guided').

gnosis_principles.description: Executing a quick port or demo to establish a baseline and guide subsequent rational technical decisions.
Evaluating performance not just by raw speed, but by the architectural overhead (locks/unlocks) of the underlying system APIs.
Advocating for open, cross-platform standards (like OpenGL) to ensure the viability of future software generations.

heritage_patterns: Porting core engine logic across disparate OS architectures (Win32 to Rhapsody/OpenStep).
Merging divergent codebase branches (QuakeWorld into Quake 2) for feature parity and stability.
Bypassing high-level abstraction layers to achieve direct hardware/screen access for performance.

dpo_pairs.prompt: How did Carmack feel about the Quake port for WWDC initially?
dpo_pairs.chosen: He was initially unaware of any such plan, stating he had only planned to support Quake 2 on the platform later in the year, but decided to 'steal some time' to implement it quickly.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He had been planning the port for a long time and was excited to show it at WWDC.

dpo_pairs.prompt: Why might the Rhapsody port be faster than the Win32 version in the future?
dpo_pairs.chosen: Because the direct-to-screen API in Rhapsody does not require the locks and unlocks necessary for Direct Draw, and it avoids DirectSound penalties.
dpo_pairs.rejected: Because Apple's hardware is fundamentally faster than Windows PCs.

dpo_pairs.prompt: What is the current state of the Quake port mentioned in the .plan file?
dpo_pairs.chosen: It is a port of the research codebase merging QuakeWorld into Quake 2 and currently only supports network games.
dpo_pairs.rejected: It is a fully completed retail version of Quake that supports both single-player and multiplayer.
